items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PHP-CFH-26-001, Public Health Dental Program Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner, Public Health and Paramedic Services, provided an update on the Public Health Dental Program and how the introduction of the Federal Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) has impacted the Public Health Dental Program and overall dental health in the Region. Dr. Wang noted that Public Health staff have assisted Waterloo Region residents to register for the CDCP where eligible but that barriers to obtaining care still exist, including co-payments, treatment delays, and challenges in obtaining approval for more complex care. She noted that Healthy Smiles Ontario is now less widely accepted by dental care providers now that the CDCP has come into effect, and that this shift has increased pressures on residents seeking dental care and created more complexity for both residents and staff navigating coverage.

Dr. Wang highlighted that while federal and provincial programs are essential, they do not fully resolve local access barriers and gaps remain for vulnerable residents, often leaving the Public Health Dental Clinic as the only option for care.

Received for information.

items.title: PHP-HPE-26-004, 2025 Public Health Infection Prevention and Control and Safe Water Inspections Report
notes:
Dr. Wang provided an update on Public Health's inspection programs for infection prevention and control, safe drinking water, and recreational water, noting that these programs are an important part of Public Health's mandate to protect residents by reducing preventable risks in work, learning, and recreational settings. She noted Public Health's role as both regulator and partner to support operators and service providers in meeting provincial requirements while taking enforcement action when needed.

Dr. Wang noted that demand for inspection programs continues to increase as the number of premises requiring inspection grows and the number of service requests, including complaints, grows. She also highlighted that Public Health uses a risk-based approach to prioritize inspections, monitoring, education, and regulatory activities where the potential for illness or injury is greatest.

The Committee recognized the importance of prevention and acknowledged the hard work of Public Health.

C. James joined the meeting at 2:48 pm.

Received for information.

items.title: CSD-HOU-26-007, Affordable Housing Refinancing Policy Framework Exemption
notes:
Ryan Pettipiere, Director, Housing Services, provided an overview of the report and highlighted that Victoria Park Homes has been awarded $5 million in capital funding for repair and retrofit of one its affordable housing properties from Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC), in the form of a forgivable loan. He noted that the Region of Waterloo's Affordable Housing Refinancing Policy only permits a provider to encumber a property at 90% of its value, and that in receiving a $5 million loan, Victoria Park Homes would exceed this threshold.

R. Pettipiere explained that staff recommend that Victoria Park Homes be granted an exemption to this policy, noting that this provider is in good standing both financially and operationally. He also noted that CMHC's policy allows a provider to encumber the value of a property up to 120%.

R. Pettipiere highlighted that staff will undertake a thorough review the existing Affordable Housing Refinancing Policy to determine if the current 90% threshold should be updated.

In response to the Committee, R. Pettipiere noted that the Region sits behind the Federal government in the security hierarchy following postponement agreements.

The Committee emphasized its support for a full policy review given that the context within which the policy operates has evolved over time. 

In response to the Committee, R. Pettipiere confirmed that the CMHC loan has a 10-year term that stipulates that properties must be maintained as affordable housing units for the term duration, also noting that other funding agreements in place will ensure that Victoria Park Homes continues to provide affordable housing beyond the 10-year period, in addition to Victoria Park Homes' own mandate as a not-for-profit.
